title: The lighthouse keeper
paragraphs: For thirty years, Pak Umar had looked after the old lighthouse on the rocky point. Every evening he climbed the narrow stairs, cleaned the lens and lit the lamp. Fishermen {{1}} on that light to find their way home, and he had never once let it go out.

One stormy night, the generator {{2}} without warning. The tower fell dark, and Pak Umar knew that several boats were still at sea. He felt a moment of pure {{3}}, but he did not stop to think about it. He ran to the storeroom and found an old oil lamp that had not been used for {{4}}.

His hands were {{5}} with cold as he carried it up the stairs. He placed it in front of the lens and turned the flame as high as it would go. The light was weak, but the lens made it {{6}} enough to reach the water.

An hour later, the first boat came {{7}} into the harbour. By morning, every crew was home. The fishermen climbed the hill to thank him, and Pak Umar, who disliked fuss, simply {{8}} and went back to cleaning the lens.
